proposals.title: Reviewed feedback: Compose Anthropic-style review layers into TIED (Claude Code comparison)
proposals.summary:
Upstream methodology improvement derived from docs/comparisons/claude-code-team-code-review-vs-tied.md (2026-10-17). External study: Anthropic "Solving code review at Anthropic" (Oct 2026) — compose-don't-replace; do not treat PR bots or article metrics as TIED authority.

Gaps called out in TIED core today:
- Review convergence: round cap, diff-only re-review, repeated-finding suppression — ad hoc in skills, not checklist/MCP receipts (matrix disposition: Gap).
- Path-scoped review guidance (REVIEW.md-style) — not a standard TIED pattern (client-owned optional).
- Risk-tier human approval automation — intent aligns via assurance profiles / depth_tier / consequence ladder; no shipped classifier for approver touchpoints (Gap automation).

Recommended phased improvements (recommendations only; each behavior-changing phase needs its own sponsor REQ/CITDP):
- Phase 1 (Loop 1): Pre-handoff verification charter — executable checks + evidence before PR/commit (doc-first).
- Phase 2 (Loop 1): Risk-tier playbook mapping assurance profiles and depth_tier to human review attention (advisory; never auto-approve costly choices).
- Phase 3 (Loop 2): Review convergence policy — round cap, diff-only re-review, class-level fixes; measure via operational observations.
- Phase 4 (Loop 3): Incident/revert evaluation corpus with explicit denominators and stop criteria (compose closed QMM machinery).
- Phase 5 (Composable): Client DevOps appendix for PR/CI/release fields — client-owned, not TIED core.

Explicit non-adoptions preserved: mandatory finding voter gate, zero-human merge for costly paths, PR-only workflow replacing LEAP/checklist, merge queue/flags as TIED core.

Next routing: Kaizen analysis digest / Loop 3 experiment bridge when sponsor promotes; optional matrix row for PR-centric review remains deferred (REQ-TIED_METHODOLOGY_COMPOSITION_MATRIX).

review.rationale: Outreach discovery from Claude Code team review comparison; queue LEAP proposal for phased compose-don't-replace improvements (each behavior-changing phase still needs its own REQ/CITDP).
